description.text: The L-xylulose reductase family comprises enzymes that catalyze the NADPH-dependent reduction of various sugars and alpha-dicarbonyl compounds. Members of this family participate in the uronate cycle of glucose metabolism and may contribute to cellular osmoregulation in renal tubules by producing xylitol, an osmolyte. Some family members also metabolize endogenous carbonyl compounds, such as those derived from lipid peroxidation, and may play a role in xenobiotic metabolism. The family belongs to the broader short-chain dehydrogenases/reductases (SDR) superfamily, known for their involvement in the metabolism of steroids, prostaglandins, and xenobiotics.

ec.description: ENZYME is a repository of information relative to the nomenclature of enzymes. It is primarily based on the recommendations of the Nomenclature Committee of the International Union of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (IUBMB) and it describes each type of characterized enzyme for which an EC (Enzyme Commission) number has been provided.
